description: Authentication proves identity (who); authorization decides permissions (what). 401 vs 403 in HTTP.
Server-side state keyed by a random id in a cookie. Revoked by deleting it.
A cookie JavaScript cannot read, so XSS cannot steal it. Combine with `Secure` and `SameSite`.
A long-lived, revocable credential used only to obtain new short-lived access tokens.
OAuth delegates access to APIs (access token); OpenID Connect adds identity (ID token). Use Authorization Code + PKCE.
WebAuthn credential bound to the site: the server stores a public key, so there is no password to phish or leak.
